clue.text: Flight path of early aircraft

parts.note: a flight can be a short journey, a trip
a path or narrow road is a lane

explanation.surface: Someone describes the route flown by a pioneering aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight path' reads as one aviation phrase, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-winged aeroplane was a design seen in the early years of powered flight, so it is an example of early aircraft.

clue.text: Spent two notes at gala

parts.note: E and F are two notes of the musical scale
a gala is a festive celebration, a fete

explanation.surface: Someone paid out a couple of banknotes at a festive event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spent' looks like money being paid out but means exhausted; 'notes' are musical, not banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means worn out and lacking vigour, the sense of spent as exhausted.

clue.text: Collect up jumble in efficient fashion

definitions.text: Collect up jumble in efficient fashion

parts.words: Collect up jumble in efficient fashion
parts.note: the clue reads like a jumble-sale chore, but describes gathering scattered pieces and fitting them neatly together

explanation.surface: A volunteer is told to gather the jumble-sale goods smartly.
explanation.definitionFit: To put together or gather into one place is the plain meaning of collecting things up in an orderly way.

clue.text: One may take this battle formation

indicators.note: a formation is an arrangement, so the letters of battle are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Soldiers are told one army might adopt this arrangement for fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' suggests a military objective, but it means swallowing medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill is something a patient swallows, so it is what one may take.

clue.text: Undirected commercial break

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, shortened to ad
a break or split is a rift

explanation.surface: A TV advertising break that has no clear direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commercial break' reads as one TV phrase, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drifting without guidance or aim is undirected, like a boat loose on the water.

clue.text: Worshipped bustle and colour

parts.note: bustle or fuss is ado
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone was idolised along with busy activity and bright colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere or love deeply is a synonym of worshipped, past tense in both.

clue.text: A ship taking trouble in attack

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A vessel in difficulty is under assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To set upon violently is a verb synonym of attack.

clue.text: An example of reduced activity?

parts.note: less means reduced or smaller in amount
on means happening or active, as in what's on

explanation.surface: A clue asks what illustrates a slowing-down of activity.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'An example' is something to learn from, not a sample.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson can be a cautionary example to learn from, as in let that be a lesson.

clue.text: A light sleeper, always arriving late for his job

definitions.text: A light sleeper, always arriving late for his job

parts.words: A light sleeper, always arriving late for his job
parts.note: the clue sounds like a dozy employee who is always tardy, but describes someone whose shift begins when evening falls and who sleeps by day

explanation.surface: A dozy employee is perpetually late for work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone employed on a shift after dark always starts late in the day and sleeps in daylight.

clue.text: Left in carriage and pair

indicators.note: the clue says the left goes in the carriage, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a coupe is a type of carriage

explanation.surface: A carriage and its two horses are left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things together form a twosome, so the word is a synonym of pair.

clue.text: In theory he wants the best

definitions.text: In theory he wants the best

parts.words: In theory he wants the best
parts.note: read as someone who claims to want the best but may not in practice; really it is a person who pursues perfection in principle

explanation.surface: Someone says he wants the best, at least in theory.
explanation.definitionFit: A person driven by lofty principles and perfection rather than practicality pursues the best.

clue.text: Such a twist of fate can't be described as hard cheese

definitions.text: Such a twist of fate can't be described as hard cheese

indicators.note: a twist rearranges something, so the letters of fate are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A stroke of bad luck is said not to count as hard cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard cheese' is British slang for bad luck; this soft Greek cheese is not a hard one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek brined cheese is soft and crumbly, so it cannot be called a hard cheese.

clue.text: Show how a student may be financed

definitions.meaning: a public display of art or goods

definitions.text: how a student may be financed
definitions.meaning: a scholarship-style grant awarded to a student at some British universities and schools

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the word is also an award paying for a student's studies.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a public display and a type of scholarship paid to a student.

clue.text: Feel very low about tropical disease

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters of the phrase are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone feels depressed while suffering from a tropical illness.
explanation.definitionFit: The mosquito-borne viral illness found in tropical Africa and South America is a tropical disease.

clue.text: No energy and lacking any inclination?

definitions.meaning: whimsically, without a list or lean, as a ship without any tilt

explanation.definitionFit: The word means lethargic, and read in parts means without a tilt or lean.

clue.text: Move to a new country home

definitions.text: Move to a new country home

parts.words: Move to a new country home
parts.note: reads like shifting to a rural house, but means relocating one's home to another nation

explanation.surface: Someone is moving to a new house in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave one's own nation and settle in another is to relocate home abroad.

clue.text: Suffer changing rig with first mate

indicators.note: changing alters the order of the letters of rig

parts.note: Eve was Adam's mate, the first woman

explanation.surface: A sailor suffers while altering a ship's rig with the first mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first mate' looks nautical, but means Eve, the first wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To mourn or feel sorrow is to suffer distress.

clue.text: Fitting task for a puzzle enthusiast?

definitions.text: Fitting task for a puzzle enthusiast?

parts.words: Fitting task for a puzzle enthusiast?
parts.note: fitting means suitable, but also literally fitting pieces together into a picture

explanation.surface: A suitable job for someone who loves puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture puzzle of interlocking pieces is literally a task of fitting things together.

clue.text: Clare Short's sort of music?

indicators.note: sort here means a rearrangement, so the letters of the politician's name are sorted anew

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: What kind of music might the British politician Clare Short enjoy?
explanation.walkthrough: Clare Short was a British Labour cabinet minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Music written for or played by a full symphonic ensemble is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Carried out shoe repairs as listed

definitions.meaning: leaned over to one side, said of a ship

explanation.definitionFit: The word means having put new heels on shoes, and leaned over as a ship does.

clue.text: Lapped and beaten

definitions.meaning: drank or touched with the tongue

explanation.definitionFit: The word means touched with the tongue, and informally defeated soundly.

clue.text: One rejecting a knight's title? It's a bloomer!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: rejecting means turning back, so the title is read backwards

parts.note: Sir is the title given to a knight

explanation.surface: A man turns down a knighthood, which is a big blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake, but here it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that flowers is a bloomer, and this one is a common garden flower.

clue.text: It brings about a military rising

definitions.text: It brings about a military rising

parts.words: It brings about a military rising
parts.note: reads like the cause of an armed uprising, but describes the bugle call that gets soldiers out of bed

explanation.surface: Something provokes an army revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call sounded at dawn wakes soldiers, so it brings about their getting up.

clue.text: Subject in a stiff examination?

parts.note: a stiff examination sounds like a hard test, but here stiff is slang for a dead body examined at a post-mortem

explanation.surface: A student sits a demanding exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead body is the subject examined at a post-mortem, and stiff is slang for one.

clue.text: Very strange verse on love

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd, so the letters of verse are rearranged

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A very odd poem about love.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase is a chatty intensifier meaning very, as in thanks ever so much.

clue.text: Present is perfect ring to wife

parts.note: best means perfect or finest
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A perfect ring is a gift for one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To give or confer formally is to present something to someone.
